sources.note: Exact id, culture kind, approximate 1500 to 500 BCE lifetime and historical-basemaps provenance.

sources.title: Human History Map research coverage ledger
sources.note: Three exact observed intervals, three border files, imported summary and missing reviewed card.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Current modern Burmese-surname paragraph is unrelated to second- and first-millennium BCE archaeology.

sources.title: Human History Map 2000 BCE borders
sources.note: Predecessor seam: tested northern points are split between Thai and Austro-Asiatic rice-culture labels.

sources.title: Human History Map 1500 BCE borders
sources.note: First exact Burmese component, its enormous bounds and point owners for 1500 to 1000 BCE.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 BCE borders
sources.note: Unchanged exact component for 1000 to 700 BCE.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 BCE borders
sources.note: Nearly unchanged component with one additional ring position for 700 to 500 BCE.

sources.title: Human History Map 500 BCE borders
sources.note: The exact target disappears at its indexed endpoint without a mapped local successor.

sources.title: Human History Map 400 BCE borders
sources.note: A broad Austro-Asiatic rice-culture layer owns nearly all tested Myanmar and Yunnan points.

sources.title: A first absolute chronology for Late Neolithic to Early Bronze Age Myanmar
sources.note: Open UCL record for 52 AMS dates, stratigraphy, pottery, burials, fauna and the Nyaunggan to Oakaie sequence.

sources.title: The Mission Archéologique Française au Myanmar: past, present and future
sources.note: Myanmar-French collaborative fieldwork, burial methods and limits of the late prehistoric dataset.

sources.title: A New Chrono-Cultural Approach to the Iron Age in Myanmar
sources.note: Oxford synthesis stresses geographically limited graves and distinguishes Chindwin and Samon sequences.

sources.title: Archaeological Studies in Myanmar
sources.note: Oxford overview links local ecosystems and resources to varied prehistoric occupation without inventing one people.

sources.title: Dating the Myanmar Bronze Age
sources.note: University repository article on Oakaie cemetery dates, preservation problems and early first-millennium BCE typology.

sources.title: Metallurgical traditions and metal exchange networks in late prehistoric central Myanmar
sources.note: Open technical study of alloys, microscopy, lead isotopes and distant copper sources.

sources.title: Late Neolithic to Early-Mid Bronze Age stone bead production
sources.note: Study of 605 roughouts, preforms, drilling waste and finished beads from settlement and burial contexts.

sources.title: Social differences in Neolithic/Bronze Age Myanmar
sources.note: Pilot strontium-isotope study of eighteen people explores locality, sex patterning and cautious kinship hypotheses.

sources.title: Living in the dry zone
sources.note: Stable-isotope research on diet, managed animals and the absence of preserved plant remains at Oakaie to Nyaunggan.

sources.title: Mobility patterning during the Neolithic and Bronze Age in north-central Myanmar
sources.note: Open 2025 strontium study compares broader Neolithic and more local Bronze Age mobility.

sources.title: An osteobiography of care at Nyaunggan
sources.note: Open study of an adolescent who survived serious childhood trauma and later lived with impairment.

sources.title: Ancient genomes document multiple waves of migration in Southeast Asian prehistory
sources.note: Science ancient-DNA study includes Oakaie individuals and warns that present languages reflect later movements.

sources.title: Bronze Age Myanmar: people from Nyaunggan cemetery
sources.note: Bioarchaeological report on excavated people rather than ethnic labels inferred from artifacts.

sources.title: Ywa Htin: Iron Age Burials in the Samon Valley
sources.note: Scholarly review anchors later Iron Age burial evidence and publication limits.

sources.title: Nyaung-gan: A Preliminary Note on a Bronze Age Cemetery
sources.note: Early field report on forty-three burials, pottery, stone ornaments and bronze objects; used with newer dating.

sources.title: Badah-lin and associated caves
sources.note: UNESCO tentative-list record for much earlier rock art, stone tools and workshop evidence in Shan State.

sources.title: Holocene environmental change at Inle Lake
sources.note: ANU palaeoenvironmental study uses pollen, charcoal and diatoms to reconstruct changing lake and vegetation histories.

sources.title: An abundance of riches: Myanmar’s many landscapes
sources.note: British Museum introduction distinguishes dry-zone, river, coast and highland environments and later political plurality.

sources.title: Pyu Ancient Cities
sources.note: UNESCO dates Pyu urban transformation from about 200 BCE, after this card, and documents later walls and waterworks.

sources.title: Myanmar’s connected cultures: a timeline
sources.note: British Museum places Pyu urban centers from about 200 BCE and emphasizes cultural plurality.

sources.title: Pyu culture collection term
sources.note: Museum catalogue separates Pyu material beginning about 200 BCE from much later Bamar history.

sources.title: Burmese: historical phonology
sources.note: Linguistic scholarship places attested Burmese at Pagan and its oldest document in 1113 CE.

sources.title: Ethnicity and loyalty in precolonial Myanmar
sources.note: Historical study dates Burmese-speaking lowland entry and written ethnonyms many centuries after the atlas interval.

sources.title: Burmese
sources.note: Glottolog identifies documented Burmese as a distinct Sino-Tibetan language, not an archaeological culture label.

sources.title: Myanmar bronzes and the Dian cultures of Yunnan
sources.note: SOAS study compares artifacts while warning that similarity does not collapse Myanmar and Yunnan traditions.

sources.title: A late second/early first millennium BCE interaction arc
sources.note: Archaeometallurgical research connects Southwest China and mainland Southeast Asia through exchange, not one ethnic territory.

sources.title: Origins of multi-cropping agriculture in Southwestern China
sources.note: Open archaeobotanical study shows varied rice, millet and wheat histories within Yunnan.

sources.title: Southbound transmission of metallurgy at Jicha, Yunnan
sources.note: Excavation and radiocarbon evidence for a distinct Yunnan settlement and cemetery around 700 BCE.

sources.title: Myanmar’s role in Iron Age interaction networks
sources.note: Glass and copper research documents later first-millennium BCE networks linking South and Southeast Asia.

sources.title: Early Food Production in Southeast Asia
sources.note: Regional synthesis supplies comparison while cautioning that domesticated-plant and animal evidence varies by site.

sources.title: Water Management in the Urban Cultural Heritage of Myanmar
sources.note: Later case studies explain wet- and dry-zone water problems; used only as comparison, not Bronze Age proof.

sources.title: Characteristics of Bronze Age in Myanmar
sources.note: Myanmar public source relays Department of Archaeology finds while retaining speculative language that requires caution.

sources.title: Metal Exchange Networks in Prehistoric Southeast Asia
sources.note: Oxford overview situates copper-bronze consumption and later iron within regional technological networks.

sources.title: Living in the middle of the edge
sources.note: Open palaeodiet study compares humans and animals while explicitly testing environmental and sex differences.

sources.title: A four-millennia sequence from Halin
sources.note: University record for Halin chronology bridging prehistoric deposits and later Pyu occupation.

sources.title: A Thousand Years before Bagan
sources.note: Cambridge chapter explains radiocarbon evidence for Pyu cities and the limits of inscription-free dating.

proposedOverrides.summary: An evidence-aware guide to late Neolithic and Bronze Age communities inside the atlas’s vast, anachronistically named Burmese layer, with exact geometry, daily life, methods and later Pyu/Bamar distinctions.
